_about: Hard Wordemic bank. Tier 1 = Einstein first, then Genius Sundays. Tier 2 = Genius (or Hard). Tier 3 = Hard. Remove a word once it's used as an answer.

1.definition: Wasting away. Tabes dorsalis is late syphilis damaging the back columns of the spinal cord: an unsteady, stamping walk and stabbing pains.
Old word for a thin, watery, foul-smelling discharge from a wound or ulcer. In Greek myth, the blood of the gods.
Soft, rubbery lump of late (tertiary) syphilis that can form in skin, bone, liver or brain.
A nest or focus where something starts, e.g. the small central core of an osteoid osteoma, or the starting point of a stone.
Heat: one of the four classic signs of inflammation described by Celsus, with rubor, tumor and dolor.
Redness: one of the four classic signs of inflammation (rubor, calor, tumor, dolor).
Hook-shaped front tip of the parahippocampal gyrus. Uncal herniation squeezes the third cranial nerve: a blown pupil.
A ridge or mound. The agger nasi is the bump in the side wall of the nose just in front of the middle turbinate, over the frontmost ethmoid air cells.
A sheath or case, e.g. the theca cells around an ovarian follicle, which make androgens that become oestrogen.
Relating to the hands and feet, e.g. acral lentiginous melanoma on the palms, soles and nail beds.
Relating to the palm (or sole). The volar side of the wrist is the palm side, as in a volar plate injury of a finger.
A swelling or knobbly growth of the skin, e.g. rhinophyma, the bulbous nose of advanced rosacea.
Old name for malabsorption with diarrhoea and weight loss: tropical sprue, or non-tropical sprue (coeliac disease).
A sudden attack, such as a seizure or stroke. 'Ictal' means during a seizure; 'postictal' is the drowsy aftermath.
The hand, in anatomical Latin: wrist, palm and fingers together.
Plural of crus, a leg-like part. The crura of the diaphragm wrap around the oesophagus at the hiatus.
Plural of acinus: tiny berry-shaped clusters of secreting cells, e.g. in the pancreas and salivary glands.
One of the fluid-filled spiral channels of the cochlea: scala vestibuli, scala media and scala tympani.
Old word for crackles: the bubbling or crackling sounds heard through a stethoscope over fluid-filled lung.
A seam-like ridge where two halves join in the midline, e.g. the scrotal raphe or the palatine raphe.

2.definition: Major hip flexor running from the lumbar spine to the femur. Psoas sign: appendicitis clue.
Plural of naevus: moles and other benign skin marks.
Chemical class that includes pralidoxime, an antidote for organophosphate poisoning.
Thread-like filament that makes up the body of a mould.
Milky, fat-rich lymph from the gut. Leaks cause chylothorax.
Folds in the lining of the stomach, vagina or hard palate.
Fold of tissue, e.g. a knee plica that can cause pain.
Fleeting or transient, as in amaurosis fugax: brief monocular vision loss.

3.definition: Tough fibrous sheet over the skull under the scalp (galea aponeurotica).
Finger-like projections lining the small intestine. Flattened in coeliac disease.
Loss of normal gut movement without a physical blockage.
Thread-like structure, e.g. the filum terminale at the end of the spinal cord.
A drop. Guttate psoriasis has drop-shaped spots.
Rounded bony bump, e.g. torus palatinus in the roof of the mouth.
